text:
Provenance confirmed, with one caveat on your planned "rendered from a photograph in Nick's files" wording (answers 1–5 below).

(1) YES. All seven 1920x1440 photos are straight conversions (HEIC → JPEG, LANCZOS downscale, no crop, no retouch) of the client HEICs, each matched by pixel correlation 0.9999–1.0000. Mapping: hero.jpg ← IMG_2736; photo-coils.jpg ← IMG_1449; photo-crane.jpg ← IMG_3768; photo-drums.jpg ← IMG_1185; photo-skid.jpg ← IMG_4422; photo-warehouse.jpg ← IMG_0317; photo-yard.jpg ← IMG_8805. "Client-supplied" is all I can attest; I cannot confirm Nick took them, where, when, or on what job (no EXIF review was in scope and none of that would prove authorship anyway). Caption them as originals from his files, not as documented jobs.

(2) YES, all seven mp4s are Grok-generated (source filenames grok-<uuid>-720p.mp4, each with a Grok keyframe still). And YES, each is visibly a selective-colour re-staging of one of those same seven photos: identical composition, objects and camera angle, with colours changed (e.g. grey transformer → yellow, blue crane → black, white wrap → blue). What I can attest is "the clip reproduces the composition of a photo in the client's files"; I cannot technically prove Grok ingested that photo as its input, though it is the only plausible explanation. Your caption "Illustrative footage, rendered from a photograph in Nick's files" is defensible on that evidence; the safest phrasing is "AI-generated illustration based on a photograph in Nick's files". Please avoid "footage" alone if it could imply a camera was present. Pairs: 01-hero ↔ hero.jpg; 02-coils ↔ photo-coils; 03-crane ↔ photo-crane; 04-drums ↔ photo-drums; 05-containers ↔ photo-yard; 06-warehouse ↔ photo-warehouse; 07-yard ↔ photo-skid.

(3) Not a deliberate design choice, an artefact of the earlier run: posters 01/03–07 are the six Grok keyframe stills (1728x1152) upscaled to 1920x1280; clip 02 has no Grok still in the source, so its poster is a native 1168x768 frame grab. All seven match their clip's first frame (corr 0.985–0.996), so nothing flashes on play. If you want uniform dimensions for width/height attributes, use the new poster-0N-*-960.jpg set (all 960x640 except poster-02-coils-960.jpg at 960x631), or set width=1168 height=768 on the <video> and let the poster cover.

(4) Nothing to exclude, and nothing beyond these: the source holds exactly 7 videos, 6 Grok stills and 7 HEICs (the lead's "8 videos" was wrong). Only extra shipped files are the seven -960 posters. Minor caution: clips 03 and 07 and photos hero, photo-crane, photo-skid contain small unidentified people (faces not distinguishable); fine to use, just do not describe them as Nick or as crew.

(5) Your avoid-list is right. Complete list from the frames: crane livery "HARGIS …" and a crane maker's name (03, photo-crane); "Seacom", "CAI", "BAHRI", container numbers CNEU 1621xx and handwritten tarp text (05, photo-yard); "WFS", "DOL 3796", wall signs "…WITHOUT A SIDA BADGE" / "SCREENED CARGO" (07, photo-skid); "ONLY FOR LASHING" strap print + desiccant-bag logo (04, photo-drums); a stamped coil emblem + handwritten gauge figures (02, photo-coils); railcar reporting marks (03). Also do not name locations (rail yard, airport, port) as facts; "yard", "warehouse", "container", "railcar" as visible objects are fine.
